page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on an ARM architecture. It is powered by 32 dedicated physical cores of Microsoft's custom ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz with 1 thread per core. The instance provides 256.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). Cache allocation includes 64 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2 per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. It operates without dedicated hardware GPUs and includes no local instance storage, requiring remote storage solutions such as Azure Premium Storage.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory subsystem throughput. The instance ranks in the top 10% for large-block memory read bandwidth (436.06 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (184.19 GB/sec), as well as overall PassMark memory performance and database operations (37,163.36). Multi-core processing capabilities are strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,664.0 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 66,283.59. Single-threaded performance sits mostly in the middle 50% tier, shown by a single-core Geekbench score of 1,661.0 and stress-ng single-core rating of 2,074.99.

Without integrated x86 vector extensions (AVX/AMX) or dedicated GPU hardware, large-scale deep learning models perform moderately to poorly, as shown by prompt processing on 70B models falling in the bottom 10%. However, the massive uncached memory bandwidth and high core density deliver efficient throughput for compiled workloads, software builds, and in-memory key-value processing. The instance delivers robust resource density for memory-bound tasks without requiring high-cost specialized accelerator hardware.

The instance is best matched for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large relational or in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data analytics pipelines, and parallel compilation tasks requiring substantial memory bandwidth and dedicated ARM core performance.
